messages.text: morning. just got back from the half-six walk with biscuit, same as every morning. making a coffee now before i get into it.
early start. biscuit doesn't seem to mind the hour.
nah, she's up for anything. still has no idea what a lead is for, though. rescue greyhound. she just sort of lets it trail behind her.
a lead as a suggestion rather than a rule.
exactly. anyway, since we moved over from manchester in the spring, the walk's been different. leeds is quieter in the mornings.
you've been here a few months now.
yeah. got a day on the halden rebrand again today. slightly dreading it, if i'm honest.
rebrands can be a slog.
tell me about it. anyway, coffee's nearly done. need to shake the cobwebs off.
hope it goes smoother than you're expecting.
me too. right, better get on.
dad's still stubborn as hell up in whitby. seventy-one and won't even look at retirement flats.
sounds like he knows what he wants.
yeah, exactly. only chance i get is the sunday call at five. he actually picks up then, weirdly.
five o'clock sundays. that's specific.
mum would have been... it'll be three years in march. anyway, i need to remember to grab milk tomorrow. dog's been giving me that look.
i think i know the look.
bloody judgy spaniel. left the back door open for five seconds and he's straight into next door's bin bags.
bin bags are a delicacy to some dogs, apparently.
tell that to my shoes. also, the weather's turned again. was sunny this morning, now it's just grey drizzle.
leeds in september does that.
suppose i should be grateful it's not snowing yet. dad's convinced it'll be a harsh winter, says his knee knows.
the knee never lies, he'd say.
and he'd be insufferably right. right, i'm off to find the remote. think the dog's hidden it under the sofa again.
good luck with that.
hey, just got in. nell's on nights again down in bristol, so i've been sent a drawing from ollie and iris. it's got a dog that looks like a potato.
a potato-dog sounds about right for that age.
yeah, it's got three legs and a smile. anyway, i keep saying i'll do the leeds half marathon in the spring, but it's one of those things.
you've mentioned that before. what's stopping you?
i'll be thirty-nine on the nineteenth of november and still haven't done a half. it's a bit pathetic really.
thirty-nine isn't old. you've got time.
i did the yorkshire three peaks last june, so it's not like i can't do distance. just the thought of all that pavement.
pavement's a different kind of misery, fair point.
exactly. and now i'm hungry and can't decide between toast or proper dinner.
toast is proper dinner if you put enough on it.
true. might do cheese on toast and call it a win.
just got back from climbing with jonah. obviously it's a thursday thing, so that's done for the week. knackered.
Sounds like a solid routine. How was it tonight?
alright, bit of a slog. my arms are shot now. had to force myself out the door, you know how it is.
I do. Better than work drinks, I imagine.
god yeah. i hate work drinks. all that forced small talk. i'd rather be home with the dog, honestly.
The dog's a better conversationalist, I take it.
definitely. less passive aggressive. anyway, got the post today. rent's gone up again. can't keep absorbing that, it's getting daft.
That's a tough one. Leeds isn't getting cheaper.
tell me about it. if i won the lottery i'd just buy a boat and fuck off. obviously that's not happening.
A boat would be a change of pace. No rent on the water.
exactly. no landlord, no neighbours. just the sea. anyway, i'm rambling. think i need tea and a quiet half hour.
Tea sounds like a good call. You've earned it after tonight.
just got in from walking the dog. bloody freezing already for september. jonah told me last night he's moving to lisbon in january.
that's a big change. are you happy for him?
yeah i think it suits him. he's always talked about it. i need to book the table for his birthday dinner by monday though, deposit thing. saturday the 19th.
plenty of time to sort it out. how's the rest of your week looking?
not bad. seeing mara tonight actually. been about two months now. her birthday's the thirty-first, halloween, she hates it. sorry, the thirtieth. always get that wrong.
halloween birthdays do seem to annoy people. does she have a party planned?
not sure yet. i'll ask her. anyway, i'm starving, might make some toast.
toast for lunch. classic.
it's efficient. what else. oh the central heating made that clanking noise again. need to get someone in.
plumbers are hard to get hold of these days. good luck with that.
hey sophie. just got in from a run, knackered. then did the sunday call.
the sunday call sounds like it went long.
yeah, dad fell yesterday. spent the night in hospital, he's home now. kept me on the phone for ages.
that must have been unsettling. how is he doing?
stiff and bruised but stubborn. i keep thinking about him being on his own up there, you know.
it's hard when they're far away. did you manage to sort anything practical today?
sent the dinner deposit this morning, so that's done. at least one thing off the list.
a small win. and you said you did 10k before the call?
yeah, did 10k this morning, my usual sunday run, so i was knackered before i even picked up the phone. but it cleared my head a bit.
does it bring up your mum at all?
i'd rather stay on my dad, if that's alright.
still up. couldnt sleep. brain just wont shut up tonight.
It's late. Anything on your mind or just one of those nights?
just one of those. so low tonight, you know. picked up the dispossessed again. that old comfort read.
That book always feels like coming home. How many times have you read it now?
lost count. it's the one i go back to when i need something solid. like a brick wall to lean on.
Sounds like you need that tonight. Anything else helping?
weirdly, i had this stupid little fantasy earlier. like, a riso press in a unit by the canal. you know, just daft. [laughs] nah, forget it.
A riso press by the canal doesn't sound daft. It sounds like a nice image.
yeah, maybe. just me and a stack of paper and that smell of ink. easier than real life.
Real life does feel heavier sometimes. Is the book helping you settle at all?
a bit. shevek's just landed on urras. that whole scene where everything's too bright and too much. hits different at 11pm.
It would. Everything's sharper when you're tired and a bit low.
exactly. anyway. probably should try and shut my eyes again. this is pointless.
It's not pointless. But if you want to try, I'll be here if you're still awake.
fucking hell, i'm wiped. barely slept all week, just one of those.
A week of bad sleep sounds rough. What's been keeping you up?
the presentation, you know. client thing i've been stressing over for ages.
And how did it go?
went alright actually. client loved it, and dee, my manager, actually said well done in front of everyone. took me by surprise.
That's a good sign. Dee doesn't sound like the praise-easily type.
no, she's not. proper hardarse usually. so that was weirdly nice.
Nice but unexpected. Are you celebrating tonight?
nah, just going home, walk the dog, crash early. i've done the burning-the-candle-at-both-ends thing before and it nearly broke me. won't take a job now where i can't leave at six.
A six o'clock boundary sounds sensible after that week.
exactly. plus the dog needs his evening walk no matter what.
He keeps you honest, then.
he does. better than any alarm clock. right, i'm off to feed him.
Enjoy the quiet evening. You've earned it.
knee's been twinging since the 10k last sunday. booked physio, tuesday four o'clock.
that's quick. hope it's nothing serious.
nah, just old man stuff. jonah made dinner last night, was actually decent. he's been getting into it.
jonah cooking. that's a shift.
yeah, he's been watching those youtube chefs. bit of a revelation.
what did he make?
some kind of miso glazed thing. worked out.
sounds good.
listen, callie's getting married in december. got the invite. haven't answered.
that's a lot. how are you feeling about it?
my gran was quaker. she never forced decisions. just sat with them till they settled. so that's what i'm doing.
that makes sense.
don't bring the callie thing up, i'm not ready.
understood.
cheers. anyway, this rain's doing my head in.
it's been relentless.
tell me about it. dog's refusing to go out.
morning. fuck, i'm wrecked. was up till two on the portfolio.
two in the morning is brutal. coffee or tea first?
tea, already got one. also realised i've been saying mara's birthday wrong in my head — it's the thirtieth, not the thirty-first. she'd kill me.
good catch. she'd probably have let you hear about it.
yeah, exactly. anyway, i need to start applying for jobs, properly. not just faffing about on linkedin.
what's the hardest part about starting?
the portfolio itself, honestly. i'm basically married to my laptop at this point.
sounds like a long-term relationship.
don't give me a pep talk, ask me one proper question instead. one good one.
all right. what would make you feel like the portfolio is finished enough to send out?
if i could just get the case study for that one project to read like a story, not a spec sheet. that's the blocker.
what's missing from the story right now?
the bit where i explain why i chose the stupid approach i chose, instead of just showing the pretty pictures. always skip that.
and that's the part that makes it human.
yeah. suppose i should write that down before i forget.
hey. just got back from a walk. nell texted earlier—she's been made ward sister. proper proud of her.
that's brilliant for her. she must be chuffed.
yeah, she deserves it. dad's staying at hers for now, till he's a bit steadier. bit of a shuffle.
sounds like a lot of moving parts at the moment.
nell mentioned he's thinking of selling the house. not sure how i feel about that, honestly. feels a bit final.
it's a lot to take in, especially secondhand.
physio went fine today, actually. knee's miles better than it was. i rested it sunday instead of running, which felt weird but helped.
good to hear it's improving. sensible call to take a day off.
yeah, well, i can't keep ignoring it. supposed to be getting a takeaway tonight, but i can't decide what.
tough choice. what are you in the mood for?
something that doesn't take much thought. had a long day at the desk, just want to switch off.
fair enough. hope you find something decent.
cheers. i'll probably end up with a pizza. standard.
can't go wrong with a classic.
fucking hell. what a day. i haven't even sat down properly, just been pacing round the flat with the dog looking at me like i've lost it.
sounds like a rough one.
dee kept adding bits to the spec, you know, scope creep, and i just lost it a bit. she's got this thing where every email has another "oh and also". so we had a proper row about it.
that's draining.
yeah. jo's been brilliant though, actually. she's the one at halden who's been helping me wrangle it all back into shape. not jonah, different person. thank god.
glad someone's on your side.
i was supposed to go climbing thursday but i just sat here answering emails instead. didn't even make it to the wall. and then i didn't sleep again, so i'm basically running on tea and stubbornness.
what's the one thing you'd want to change about how dee communicates those additions?
see, that's what i mean. it's not the additions, it's the way they just appear without any warning. if she'd just say "look, i need this" in one go, fine. but it's the drip-drip-drip.
morning. knackered. went to saltburn with mara at the weekend, did a run along the front on sunday. felt good, actually. sea air.
Saltburn's a nice spot. Was it your first time there?

yeah, first time. bit of a kitsch seaside vibe, but the beach was decent. there's an old print shop there, proper letterpress stuff. made me think of the riso thing, you know. making stuff with your hands, no screens.
I can see why that would appeal to a designer.
told mara about my mum properly, first time in ages. don't know why it came up, just did. felt weird.
You sound like you're still grieving your mum.
mm.
That's a heavy thing to share, even with someone close.
yeah. she didn't pry, which was good. just listened. we had fish and chips after.
Sounds like a decent weekend, despite the weight.
it was alright. dog was wrecked after the run, slept the whole way back in the car.
knackered. went for a run this morning, eight miles. didn't think i'd bother but the weather was alright for once.
eight miles is a solid distance. how'd the legs hold up?
not bad actually. registration for the leeds half opens in november. if i can do the three peaks i can do thirteen, right? that's the logic anyway.
seems reasonable. you've got a couple of months to decide.
yeah. been thinking about other stuff too. might go to the wedding after all. let it settle first, see how i feel.
the one you mentioned before? what changed your mind?
nothing drastic. just woke up and thought maybe. my dad's still at nell's so there's that in the background.
still at nell's. that's been going on a while.
yeah. it's fine, just one of those things. anyway, callie's been moping on the sofa all day. think she missed me while i was out.
dogs know. they always know when you've been gone.
tell me about it. she's got a sixth sense for the sound of my keys.

patched: S06: Tom says 10k explicitly; Sophie's mum question made neutral (mum is dead)
